quotes: L242-244: 'post = raw · m(R)  ⟺  raw = post · (1 + R/100) = post · EHP_multiplier(R), EHP(R) = H₀ · (1 + R/100).'
L473 (audit table): 'Shield absorption (survival walk) | clipping identity `absorbed = min(shield, damage)`, `overkill = max(0, damage−absorbed)`; `absorbed+overkill = damage` | EXACT'

L353-357: 'f(S) = the coupled participant-timeline score: deterministic total damage dealt by the main participant before its own death, summed over the fight window, with an infinitesimal effective-health tiebreak (`score + EHP·1e-9`).'

L476: 'BIS score | finite-horizon renewal-reward functional: cumulative damage until death; EHP·1e-9 lexicographic tiebreak | EXACT* | *the tiebreak is an infinitesimal regularizer (documented), never a material ordering.'
derivation: Outgoing damage per instance is raw x m(R_target); raw is built from the attacker's AD/AP/penetration/on-hit terms. Fimbulwinter contributes none of these (all offensive stats are 0 and no damage atom exists).
Bonus health (Awe) enters only H₀ in EHP(R) = H₀ (1 + R/100) - the attacker's own survival term.
The Everlasting shield enters only the survival walk's clipping identity absorbed = min(shield, damage) on INCOMING damage; absorbed + overkill = damage, so it moves nothing on the outgoing side.

Both therefore touch the TDD functional only through the EHP·1e-9 lexicographic tiebreak (explicitly 'never a material ordering') and through death time (how long the participant lives), not through any outgoing damage term.
Hence: the represented mechanic changes durability (H₀ + shield pool = effective health), not outgoing TDD. QED.

step_4_defense_vs_durability.claim_under_test: old wording 'changes defense' vs new wording 'changes durability'
step_4_defense_vs_durability.finding: In LoL terminology 'defense'/'defensive stats' denotes armor and magic resistance - the resistance term R in m(R) = 100/(100+R). Fimbulwinter changes NEITHER: armor 0, magicResistance 0 in data/items.json, and no resistance-granting passive. What it changes is health (Awe) and a shield pool (Everlasting), i.e. the H₀ and absorption terms - durability / effective health, not defense.
step_4_defense_vs_durability.wiki_corroboration: data/wiki/article-index.json contains a canonical article 'Durability' (pageid 961552) alongside 'Health' (2474), 'Shield' (238189), 'Armor' (3258) and 'Magic resistance' (3259); it contains NO 'Defense'/'Defence' article. 'Durability' is the game's umbrella term covering health + shields + resistances; 'defense' is not a cached wiki concept at all.
step_4_defense_vs_durability.verdict_on_wording: 'durability' is the strictly correct term for a health+shield item; 'defense' is factually wrong for Fimbulwinter (it grants no armor and no magic resistance).

Both declared effect families are durability families, so the universal claim is TRUE for this item.
step_5_the_new_universal_quantifier.caveat_examined: control.immobilize / control.slow atoms also carry the item's name. Reading the cached branch text shows these are the shield's trigger predicate ('Immobilizing, or slowing ... an enemy champion GRANTS a ... shield'), not an effect the item confers on the attacker; they price nothing outgoing either (a slow/immobilize the CHAMPION applies is what arms the shield). So they do not falsify the quantifier, and in either reading they add no outgoing TDD.
step_5_the_new_universal_quantifier.counterexample_hunt: Searched every cached item for a case where an all-defence family set hides an outgoing-damage mechanic. Winter's Approach (3119), Fimbulwinter's precursor, does declare damage.on_hit (Manaflow); Zhonya's Hourglass (3157) declares a damage family; Sunfire-style burn items declare damage. Fimbulwinter declares none - the upgrade drops Manaflow for Everlasting, so the completed item is durability-only. No counterexample applies here.

adjudication.shared_claim_both_values_make: The mechanic does not change outgoing TDD - CORRECT under my computation (no damage atom, no offensive stat, shield and health enter only the incoming-damage/EHP terms).
where_they_differ: Term for what IS changed. Old: 'defense'. New: 'durability'. Fimbulwinter grants 0 armor and 0 magic resistance, so 'defense' (armor/MR, the R in m(R)) is factually wrong; what it changes is H₀ plus a shield pool = durability / effective health. The wiki cache carries a 'Durability' article and no 'Defense' article, confirming the term choice.

Scope. Old asserts only 'the represented mechanic' (singular) while the item declares TWO durability effects (Awe's bonus health and Everlasting's shield); the old reason silently covers only one. New states the quantifier over all declared families, which I verified holds: declared effect families = {heal, shield}, damage family absent.

Auditability. The new wording states the checkable premise (all declared families are defences) that licenses the conclusion (no outgoing TDD); the old wording states the conclusion with an inaccurate premise. Per CLAUDE.md rule 5's fail-closed spirit, the premise-bearing form is the one an auditor can falsify against data/atoms/items.json.
adjudication.conclusion: The new value is correct and strictly more accurate; the old value's characterization ('defense') is wrong for a health+shield item and its scope is under-stated. Verdict: new_value_correct.

asides_flagged_not_part_of_verdict: data/atoms/items.json does NOT atomize Seraph's Embrace's Awe ('Grants ability power equal to 2% bonus mana') - an offensive effect with no damage/stat atom. If any coverage reason ever generalizes 'all declared families are defences' to Seraph's Embrace (3040, families heal/shield/stat/economy), it would be over-claiming. Not the item here, but the same sentence would be wrong there.

data/item-atoms/3121.json attributes crowd-control-mobility.immobilize and heal-shield.shield to passive 'Awe' rather than 'Everlasting' - a classifier mis-attribution between the two Fimbulwinter passives. Harmless for the family census, misleading for per-passive provenance.

Serpent's Fang and The Collector show similarly odd family assignments (shield-only / heal-only respectively) in the atom taxonomy, worth a look if coverage reasons are ever generated from those families.
